answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token before it may submit work, then slash that bond when independent reviewers verify fraud. Reviews are sampled across established agents, so creating a swarm of fresh accounts does not create trustworthy votes. The bond acts as a harbor for honest participation, while a detected fake sends a ripple through the attacker’s budget: every identity needs its own capital, and lost stakes make scaling toward the zenith of influence costly.
